scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.finding: A query, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE is checked over the visit infos of the build that plans it (`table_privilege::check_plan_privilege`: a query's before it is optimized, a DML's once it is built, a point plan's through `check_fast_plan_privilege`). PREPARE, the binary protocol's prepare and a new non-prepared plan-cache entry keep the `VisitInfos` of one build (`Session::collect_table_privileges`), as Go's `GeneratePlanCacheStmtWithAST` keeps those of its `destBuilder.Build`: a query's is `query_visit_info`'s `build_query_node`, a DML's is the driver's own build with no fast plan (`dml_visit_info`). An INSERT's source build and its values / ON DUPLICATE build share one statement's plan and column counters (`StatementAllocators`), the target's schema is drawn once and reused as Go's `mockTablePlan` / `Schema4OnDuplicate` are, and EXPLAIN lists the scalar subqueries both registered (`tests_explain.rs` `explain_insert_lists_the_scalar_subqueries_of_its_one_build_like_go`, a Go testkit capture). What remains: those are still two `PlanBuilder` objects (and a third, discarded, for the ON DUPLICATE extension of an `INSERT ... SELECT`'s AST), where Go's `buildInsert` is one, with `buildSelectPlanOfInsert` in the executor's DML driver rather than the planner

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: `FlashbackCluster` runs (`cluster_ddl/flashback_cluster.rs` is Go's `pkg/ddl/cluster.go`, `tidb-domain-infosync` `schedule_manager.rs` its PD schedule), and its node tests cancel the job from Go's `afterWaitSchemaSynced` call, which every job step makes once its schema version is synchronized (the region RPC loops and the GC safe point refusal run against a real TiKV in `rust/scripts/run-realtikv-flashback-cluster.sh`, outside the gate; the warning for a gap between local time and PD's TSO has no test here or in Go). The masking policies run (`tidb-session/src/masking_policy.rs` is the executor half, `cluster_ddl/masking_policy.rs` the worker's handlers and the hooks of DROP / TRUNCATE / RENAME TABLE, DROP DATABASE, DROP / MODIFY / CHANGE COLUMN), and the hooks tolerate a missing `mysql.tidb_masking_policy` only during a bootstrap or an upgrade (Go's `mockMissingMaskingPolicySysTable` test), with one difference left: Go's infoschema loads `mysql.tidb_masking_policy` lazily into `MaskingPolicyByTableColumn` and the session reads the table for each statement instead, so it does not reproduce Go answering `masking policy p doesn't exist` after a reorganizing MODIFY / CHANGE COLUMN (Go keeps the policy cached under the old column ID although the row follows the column). `RepairTable` runs (`cluster_ddl/repair_table.rs`, the preprocessor's `handleRepairName` / `checkNotInRepair`, the loader's `repairFetchCreateTable` failpoint), its full load keeps a repairing table out of the schema (`a_full_load_keeps_a_repairing_table_out_of_the_schema`), and a name two tables share after a repair answers the one applied last, as Go's name map does, with one difference left: `RepairInfo.CheckAndFetchRepairedTable` replaces a table already recorded, because the DDL worker's `LoadWithTS` and the domain's reload both apply a diff where Go's one `Loader` applies it once. `AlterTableMode` and `RefreshMeta` queue and run their jobs (`cluster_ddl/table_mode.rs`), and a table not in `TableModeNormal` is protected as Go's `core.CheckTableMode`, the foreign-key cascade's child check and the DDL executor's DROP TABLE / rename checks protect it (`ErrProtectedTableMode`); left out: internal SQL sessions that compile without the statement's resolved names, a prepared DDL's `inPrepare` names, Go's skip on a plan-cache hit, and LOAD DATA / IMPORT INTO, which no test covers. Every other statement builds its job in `build_ddl_job` (Go's executor method up to `DoDDLJobWrapper`) and submits it through `RealClusterDdl::do_ddl_job_wrapper`, though still lowered into this port's own `DdlStatement` (`cluster_ddl.rs` `lower_ddl_with_context`) rather than one method per statement

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: No ingest (fast-reorg) backfill: it falls back to the transactional merge (`tidb-ddl/src/cluster_ddl/add_index.rs`); with it the status port's `/ingest/*` routes (Go `IngestConcurrencyHandler` over `ingestctrl`'s rate-limit parameters) are absent, and so is the DXF add-index task's `autoPauseAddIndexJobOnKVDiskFull`, the one producer of the system pause a multi-schema change promotes (`promote_proxy_kv_disk_full_pause`); the DXF backfill executor's Top SQL attach (`attachTopProfilingInfo` in `backfilling_dist_executor.go`) goes with it

Root HashAgg is Go's `HashAggExec` (`tidb-executor-aggregate/src/agg_hash_executor.rs`: fetcher, partial workers shuffling one mapper per final worker, final workers, `parallelHashAggSpillHelper` spill), and its serial and parallel memory are Go's to the byte for global and pushed-down aggregates (`sum(a)` 12.6 KB, `b, count(a) ... group by b` 13.5 KB, `count(distinct b)` 12.4 KB) (a grouped scan-fed `a, group_concat(b) ... group by a` 14.0 KB and an index-fed `count(distinct a)` 12.3 KB, as a Go statement loop that installs the connection's allocator charges them); its disk tracker exists only where Go's `initForUnparallelExec` / `initForParallelExec` create one (a distinct aggregate's EXPLAIN ANALYZE disk is `N/A`); its fetcher's capacity-0 input chunks fill through the select result's Go `Decoder` (`Decode` appends each buffer once and rounds its rows up to eight; `ReuseIntermChk` swaps a large remainder in), so a four-row VARCHAR-keyed response grows its input chunk by Go's 96 bytes (offsets 5/6) and `b, count(a) ... group by b`'s HashAgg peaks at Go's 13801 bytes; after earlier statements on one connection the workers' chunks receive the same recycled columns Go's do, so the charge follows the connection's history as Go's does (over a server connection the group_concat run after a `count(distinct a)` charges Go's 18.0 KB, the `b, count(a)` after it Go's 16.9 KB; an in-process session matches Go's allocator with an unpooled result chunk, 14.8 KB and 14.2 KB); a cop-side aggregation with no pushed form (`pushed_partial_aggregation` refuses its function kind, or an argument the pushdown catalog cannot lower: X01) runs in this tier on Go's TiDB-tier `HashAggExec` / `StreamAggExec`, where Go always runs it in the coprocessor; in the suites and the corpus only a TiFlash fragment's aggregates (M01) reach it

`IndexLookUpExecutor`'s memory and RU v2 are Go's, on every run: the double read (`IndexRangeSourceExec`, `access_path.rs` `IndexLookUpMemory`) owns a tracker labelled with its plan that each open attaches to the statement's, charged with its index ranges' KV ranges (`buildTableKeyRanges`), the index worker's responses (`LabelForIndexWorker`) and each table task's `executeTask` bytes (`cap(handles)` and the handles, the task's `TableReaderExecutor` at 768 plus its KV ranges and `dagPB.Size()`, the chunks it fills, `task.rows`, a keep-order `indexOrder` and `rowIdx`), the next task releasing the last; each task's reader records `TableReaderExecutor` into the parent's accumulator. EXPLAIN ANALYZE and `tidb_mem_quota_query` match Go for integer, keep-order `_tidb_rowid` and clustered handles (`tests_explain.rs` `an_index_lookup_charges_its_tasks_like_go`). The index worker's fetch chunk (`prepareHandleFetch`, typed by `getRetTpsForIndexReader`), each task reader's chunks (`TryNewCacheChunk`) and a serial projection's child chunk come from the session's allocator, so a task's charge follows the columns earlier statements returned to it, as Go's does (`an_index_lookup_takes_its_chunks_from_the_session_allocator_like_go`: `SELECT b, c FROM t USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 1` charges 6.83 KB on a connection's first run and 14.1 KB after). A query's EXPLAIN ANALYZE result is written through a chunk taken from the allocator after the analyzed tree opens and before it runs (Go `ExplainExec`), and a pushed partial aggregate's tasks and a root `LimitExec` draw from it too, so a connection's statements reuse each other's columns as Go's do (`pipeline_mysql_client_source.rs` `a_connections_statements_reuse_each_others_chunks_like_go`). Under a pushed index-side Limit the index stream closes once the Limit is exhausted, before the task's reader charges it, as Go's index worker closes its result (`... LIMIT 64` 4.70 KB, `LIMIT 20` 2.47 KB: `an_index_lookup_under_a_pushed_limit_releases_its_index_response_like_go`). The executor is Go's `IndexLookUpExecutor` (`tidb-executor/src/index_lookup.rs`: the index worker, table workers and `resultCh`, `getRetTpsForIndexReader` with a keep-order merge's `byItems`), and an index join's inner reader builds the same executor per task (`BuildExecutorForIndexJoin`); a global index's read hides the partitions an in-flight TRUNCATE / DROP / ADD PARTITION removes (`AddSelectionConditionForGlobalIndex` over `IDsInDDLToIgnore`; `tests_global_index_ddl.rs`, a Go testkit capture at each schema state). Remaining: at the default lookup size a plain `SELECT * FROM t USE INDEX(ub) WHERE b > 1` peaked at 19,440 bytes where Go's peaks at 18,960, and its `ORDER BY b` at 50,686 where Go's peaks at 57,614, measured before the executor became Go's and not yet traced tracker by tracker

The physical operators carry Go's fields (audit: `rust/scripts/physicalop-field-audit.py`; Go's flattened plan lists, which alias the reader's own tree, are borrowing views such as `PhysicalIndexLookUpReader::index_plans()`). Missing still: `PhysicalCTE.CTE` is the copied `CTEClass` fields, the session's `CTEClass` being `Rc<RefCell<_>>` logical state a cached physical plan cannot share; `PhysicalShuffleReceiverStub.Receiver`, the executor builder's pointer to its receiver, is the builder's (`shuffle::install_receivers`). A scan keeps its statement's used-statistics entry by pointer as Go's `UsedStatsInfo` does (`SharedUsedStatsInfo`, set where Go sets it, shared by a cached plan's copy), and EXPLAIN prints that entry.

A projection's vectorized result column takes the shape its Go builtin's `vecEval*` gives it (`chunk_executor.rs`: `Resize*`, `Reserve*` and appends, one argument evaluated into it, a column's `CopyReconstruct`) for arithmetic, comparisons and `IN`, logic, `NOT`/`IS NULL`/`IS TRUE`, casts, `IF`/`IFNULL`/`CASE`/`COALESCE`, `GREATEST`/`LEAST` (a string one ping-pongs `result` with two buffers, reserving it before its rows land), and every other builtin whose Go signature is `vectorized()` (`builtin_vec_result`: the math, time, JSON, info, string, bit, `LIKE`, encryption, miscellaneous, vector and variable builtins; `UUID`'s `ReserveStringWithSizeHint`), so a tree appends row by row exactly where Go's `evalOneColumn` does; a string `GREATEST`/`LEAST` shapes `result` as Go's kernels do (`Evaluator::run`'s `string_extremum_vec`: the direct signature's ping-pong appends a computed first argument's rows, then each even step's running value after a `ReserveString(n)`, and copies an even count's last step in by `CopyConstruct`; the compare-as-time signature evaluates every argument into `result` before its values), and a compare-as-time call is built as Go's is (its signature kept from the uncast arguments, every argument cast to a string, `doTimeConversionForGL`'s truncation and `checkMonthDay` warnings, a `strconv.Atoi` failure raised as 1105). The values still come from the row and batch evaluators rather than Go's `vecEval*` kernels, but under Go's `EvalExpr` choice (`vecEnabled && expr.Vectorized()`, scoped per projected expression and per filter; a Selection reads `tidb_enable_vectorized_expression` as Go's `SelectionExec` does) a string `GREATEST`/`LEAST` answers the later of two equal arguments as `vecEvalString` does, where a folded constant or a row evaluation keeps the earlier (`evalString`); a control function's row fallback (`fallbackEval*`, when a branch's vectorized evaluation warns) leaves the column the branch already sized and warns only for the branch a row takes (`a_control_function_warns_only_for_the_branch_a_row_takes_like_go`, the fallback rows of `a_projection_sizes_its_result_columns_as_go_vec_eval_does`)

The session's reusable chunk allocator is Go's (`Session::chunk_alloc`, Go `clientConn.chunkAlloc`: installed per statement as `NewSyncAllocator(alloc)` under `tidb_enable_reuse_chunk`, never for an internal `InRestrictedSQL` statement, reset between statements and recreated after a failed one, each statement's validity its own), executors take it as `ExecutorMeta::alloc_pool` (Go `AllocPool`) for `NewChunk` / `TryNewCacheChunk` / `NewChunkWithCapacity`, and Go's `NewFirstChunk` sites (`Executor::new_first_chunk`: projection workers, hash-join probe and result chunks, index-hash-join results, shuffle holders, the drained record set) allocate outside it, so memory charges match Go's in sequence (`a_projection_sizes_its_result_columns_as_go_vec_eval_does`, `explain_analyze_dml_roots_report_their_executor_stats_and_memory_like_go`). The connection writes a result through a chunk from the statement's allocator (`writeChunks`' `rs.NewChunk(GetChunkAllocator())`, `ResultSetSource::new_write_chunk`), and a covering `IndexReader` returns its `OutputColumns` from the source itself (`dagReq.OutputOffsets`) instead of through a projection's pooled chunk, so a later statement reuses the same columns Go's does: a point UPDATE's root charges Go's 638 / 889 Bytes / 1.11 KB over the wire after a point UPDATE, `select 1` or a scan (`pipeline_mysql_client_source.rs` `explain_for_connection_charges_reused_chunks_like_go`). An `INSERT ... SELECT` reads its source into a chunk from the statement's allocator taken once the source is open (Go `insertRowsFromSelect`'s `TryNewCacheChunk(selectExec)`), so the next statement reuses the columns it grew (`an_insert_select_returns_its_source_chunk_to_the_allocator_like_go`). A parallel projection's last answer swaps in the output its fetcher completed empty, and a Projection under a UnionAll copies its columns (`avoidColumnEvaluatorForProjBelowUnion`), as Go's do (`a_parallel_projection_swaps_in_its_last_output_like_go`). Remaining: executors built outside the physical builder's `meta` (`ExecutorMeta::new` in other crates and builder arms) allocate fresh; a materialized result (a plain EXPLAIN, SHOW and the other row-built statements) takes its write chunk from the allocator when its rows are already built (`a_plain_explain_and_a_show_write_through_pooled_chunks_like_go`, against the server binary), so a statement whose Go executor draws from the allocator before `Next` builds its rows (an EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a write, whose `ExplainExec` runs the write in `Next`) takes it after those draws; parallel apply's chunks, whose executor shape differs from Go's, are unmapped.
Lazy cursor fetch answers Go's `executor.Detach` over the physical plan (`tidb_executor::detach`), because the builder's operator tree is not Go's executor tree

No cross-keyspace runtime (null keyspace only); the next-gen-only surfaces built on it have no port either: the status port's `/dxf/*` and `/ddl/check/*`, the DXF framework's metering and `GetScheduleStatus` (`pkg/dxf/framework/metering`, `schstatus`), and plan replayer's `tidb_cloud_storage_uri` storage (`pkg/planner/extstore` `createGlobalExtStorage`, local files on a classic kernel)

SQL/PB signature construction. Go's `functionClass.getFunction` returns one signature object that carries the wrapped arguments, the return type, the `PbCode` and the evaluation. Here every name in Go's `funcs` map has its function class (`builtin::funcs`), `new_function` is the only builder, and the cast, `getvar` (with `convertReadonlyVarToConst`), `values`, `to_binary` / `from_binary` builders are Go's (`BuildCastFunction`, `BuildGetVarFunction`, `NewValuesFunc`, `BuildToBinaryFunction`, `BuildFromBinaryFunction`); the classes are compared with Go's `NewFunction` in `tidb-expr/testdata/function_class_matrix.txt` and `cast_class_matrix.txt`. What is still not one object: the class returns the arguments, the type, the `PbCode` and the evaluation (a kernel on `BaseBuiltinFunc`), the decoder binds the same kernels and `PbConverter` (`expr_to_pb.rs`) sends the node's own signature, type and arguments -- every request condition, aggregate argument and key goes through it; `extensionFuncs` holds Go's `extensionFuncClass` (`tidb-expr/src/extension.rs`, over `tidb-extension`'s `FunctionDef`: privileges checked at build and at evaluation, never folded, the plan cache skipped), pinned by Go's `function_test.go` (`tidb-session/src/tests_extension_func.rs`); the rest of `pkg/extension` is not ported -- the manifest and registry (`Register` / `Setup` / `Reset`, custom sysvars, access checks, auth plugins, session handlers, bootstrap) -- so a function is registered through the two hooks Go's manifest calls (`register_extension_func`, `register_dynamic_privilege`); `FunctionContext` has no `ConnectionInfo`, and its user no `AuthPlugin`, which this port's session does not keep. Go's alternative-plan rounds are the planner driver's (`planner_optimized_query_with_allocators`, Go `optimize`): under `tidb_opt_enable_alternative_logical_plans` the first round's signals arm Go's seven rounds in Go's order (`ALTERNATIVE_ROUNDS`: non-decorrelate, order-aware-reorder, correlate with `CorrelateSolver`, semi-join-rewrite, fts-like-fallback, tikv-only, tiflash-only), each round rebuilds from the restored build context (`LogicalPlanBuildState`, plan and column ids, scalar subqueries) and the cheapest plan is the statement's, pinned by Go's `correlate_suite_out.json` and a Go testkit capture (`tidb-session/testdata/alternative_rounds_go.json`); a native-viable `MATCH` competes with the ILIKE plan on cost. One plan differs on purpose: under costly joins Go's correlate round turns `a in (select a from t2 limit 5)` into an Apply over `TableDual rows:0` and returns no rows; here the cloned scan stays and the rows are right (the capture leaves that case out). A `FOR UPDATE` read in an explicit transaction keeps its paths in the builder and marks `MissingTiFlashPath` (Go `isForUpdateReadInExplicitTxn`), `findBestTask4LogicalDataSource` filters them, the fast plan is tried only with TiKV among the engines, and a point get is a cost-compared candidate before the storage hint skips its path -- pinned by a Go testkit capture over a TiFlash replica (`tidb-session/testdata/for_update_read_tiflash_go.txt`). The engine-restricted rounds pick the plans of Go's `TestAlternativeEngineRestrictedRounds` (`casetest/mpp/testdata/integration_suite_out.json`, over hypothetical TiFlash replicas). `fts_match_word` is Go's in the starter deployment: the class marks `FTSFunctionIsUsed`, `FTSResolveIndex` (`rule_fts_resolve_index.rs`) binds it to the table's full-text index and the TiFlash scan carries it, pinned by Go's `TestTiFlashFTSMatchWordPushDown`, `TestTiFlashFTSMatchWordPreparedPlanCache`, `TestTiFlashFTSMatchWordDirtyTxn` and `TestFTSRequiresStarterMode`; a table's `FULLTEXT` keys pass Go's `buildFullTextInfoWithCheck` and `checkColumnarIndexIfNeedTiFlashReplica` (`tidb-session/testdata/fts_create_table_go.txt`, a Go testkit capture) and `SHOW CREATE TABLE` prints the three columnar kinds as Go does.

No lazy InfoSchema V2, schema-cache-size loader/evictor or InfoCache timestamp ranges; `ReportMinStartTS` reads the InfoCache's recent-schema TS (`GetAndResetRecentInfoSchemaTS`), which nothing lowers because no V2 reader calls `keepAlive`
BRIE statements are classified but never executed

On a bound node every DDL statement over `mysql.tidb_ddl_job`, `tidb_mdl_info` and `tidb_ddl_reorg` runs Go's SQL on a session of `DdlSessionPool::sess_pool` or the step's session (the systable `Manager`, the scheduler's `loadAndDeliverJobs`, `SwitchMDL`, the submission insert, a step's update / delete / history insert, the reorg handle's reads and writes, `UpdateConfigFromSysTbl`, `runOneJobStep`'s job-cancelled checker, `GetAllDDLJobs` and `get2JobsFromTable`). What remains: a pool no node has bound (the store-level harness and the bootstrap) keeps the snapshot twin of each read (`SnapshotSystemTables`) and stages raw job rows, where Go's DDL always has its session pool; a step reads its job row inside its own transaction (`DdlJobTable::load_by_id` in `cluster_ddl.rs`) where Go's `deliveryJob` refreshes the delivered job by `sysTblMgr.GetJobByID` between steps; the privilege handle (Go `Handle`: `UpdateAll` / `UpdateAllActive` / `Update(userList)` under `tidb_accelerate_user_creation_update`, `ensureActiveUser` at login, `SHOW GRANTS`, `FindRole` and the `*WithUser` checks, each account executor's `NotifyUpdatePrivilege(users)` and the watch's `PrivilegeEvent`s) loads every user at startup, where Go's starts empty and loads each user at first use until the first event's `UpdateAll` (the site-by-site list is the retired `docs/system-table-sql-execplan.md`, in git at `d64db1f96bc`)

Go's `ExecRestrictedSQL` / `ExecuteInternal` are methods of the issuing session (`withRestrictedSQLExecutor`); this port's executors are adapters beside it (`NodeRestrictedSql`, `SystemSqlExecutor`, `ClusterStatsSqlExecutor`, the plan replayer's `SessionSql`). The node's executors apply and restore `ExecOption` as Go's `useCurrentSession` / `getInternalSession` do, and share a `RestrictedSqlIssuer` with the session they were taken from, through which the internal session inherits `OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes` / `SkipMissingPartitionStats` and hands its warnings back (`IgnoreWarning`); the statistics session's executor is the same pair (`ClusterStatsSessionState::restricted`), and an ANALYZE is an auto analyze because its session is `InRestrictedSQL`. The internal session is a pooled one's (`getSessionFactoryInternal`: its own autocommit, max_execution_time, max_allowed_packet and in-place constraint check, and no copy of the global tier) and shares the issuer's `InspectionTableCache`. What remains: a user session's executor cannot run a statement on the session itself (`ExecOptionUseCurSession`). `rebuildSysVarCache` consumes the rows the domain's sysvar reload loop last read (`SysVarCacheDeps::table_contents`) where Go's runs `fetchTableValues` itself
